title: ARM-FM: Automated Reward Machines via Foundation Models for Compositional Reinforcement Learning
claim: A foundation model compiles a task description into a structured reward automaton that guides RL, solving sparse-reward tasks where baselines fail.
layout: 2 columns: left two stacked pipeline panels, right two stacked bar charts
description: The left side has two rounded panels. The top, orange panel is 'Reward Machine Generation'. A prompt box with a gridworld screenshot feeds a central 'Foundation Model' box. Three arrows lead from it to outputs: a purple formal RM specification (states, transitions, rewards), dark code boxes with labelling functions, and teal natural-language state instructions with embeddings. The bottom, blue panel is 'RL Training'. It shows a loop linking the RL agent, the environment, a reward machine automaton (u0, u1, u2), labelling functions and FM embeddings, with the equation R_total = R_RM + R. The right side has two stacked bar charts of success rate against environment steps. The 'Baseline' chart stays near zero. The 'Ours' chart climbs to about 0.85, with stacked bars colored by Minecraft resource icons.
caption: An overview of our framework (left) and results in a complex sparse-reward environment (right). Reward Machine Generation (top-left): Given a high-level natural language prompt and a visual observation of the environment, a FM automatically generates the formal specification of the \purpletext{Reward Machine}, the executable Python code for the \codetext{labeling functions}, and the \cyantext{natural language descriptions} for each RM state. RL training (bottom-left): During the RL training loop, the \codetext{labeling functions} evaluate environment observations to update the \purpletext{Reward Machine}'s state, which provides a dense reward signal $R_t^{RM}$. The RL agent's policy receives the environment observation along with the \cyantext{embedding $\phi(\cdot)$} of the current RM state's language description, making it aware of its active sub-goal. Empirical results (right): Results in a complex sparse-reward Minecraft-based resource-gathering task from Craftium [ref], where an RL agent is unable to make progress (top), while our agent, guided by an FM-generated LARM, learns to solve the task efficiently (bottom).
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are highly sensitive to reward function specification, which remains a central challenge limiting their broad applicability. We present ARM-FM: Automated Reward Machines via Foundation Models, a framework for automated, compositional reward design in RL that leverages the high-level reasoning capabilities of foundation models (FMs). Reward machines (RMs) -- an automata-based formalism for reward specification -- are used as the mechanism for RL objective specification, and are automatically constructed via the use of FMs. The structured formalism of RMs yields effective task decompositions, while the use of FMs enables objective specifications in natural language. Concretely, we (i) use FMs to automatically generate RMs from natural language specifications; (ii) associate language embeddings with each RM automata-state to enable generalization across tasks; and (iii) provide empirical evidence of ARM-FM's effectiveness in a diverse suite of challenging environments, including evidence of zero-shot generalization.
